Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:28: The reason is as I explained: since the days are a garment for the soul, and a single day is a small portion, the measure of a small stature, of that garment - it is counted against him as though he blemished the whole year. Therefore great care is needed lest he blemish any of his days; and if, God forbid, he has blemished one, let him repent on that very day, along the lines of (Avot 2:10) "repent one day before your death," which our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Shabbat 153a) to mean that all his days are found in a state of repentance. My teacher, peace be upon him, explains that the intent is that his days should be illuminated from the secret of supernal repentance, just as during the Ten Days of Repentance, repentance repairs all the days of the year because they all return to it, so too, upon each day's individual return, they are illuminated from repentance, and they are all found repaired before the Day of Judgment of Rosh Hashanah and the Ten Days of Repentance arrives.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:29: So too Rashbi says (Vayechi 220a) - his words: "but the righteous, the pious, examine their hearts every day as though on that day they were to depart the world, and perform complete repentance before their Master, so that they need nothing further in the World to Come" - so far. What he says, "so that they need nothing further," refers to what was explained, that the image departs from a person and it depends on whether he repents or not, and likewise the matter of the documents delivered into the hands of the messengers explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:30: Let us return to our subject: it says that they judge him in Gehinnom day for day, double for one - from this we draw that since they punish him double for one, it is fitting that upon his repentance he should perform mitzvot and Torah study every day, doubly, and increase in the mitzvah of tefillin morning and evening and all that is within his power, and likewise visiting the sick, and increasing in charity, and the like of all the mitzvot of acts of kindness, and repent - for through repentance he repairs the missing days, and this is a great virtue of repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:31: Further, concerning the blemish pertaining to the days, the commentators explain that in the twelve hours of day and night, twelve permutations of YHVH revolve, one permutation per hour, and if, God forbid, one blemishes, he blemishes that particular "being" revolving in that hour; this is similar to what the pious one said (see Chovot HaLevavot, Gate of the Service of God, chapter 5), "do not rebel against your Master while He watches over you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:32: Further, the commentators explain that there are 4,320 parts in an hour, and corresponding to them, the Name of four letters revolves in the combination of its vocalization through 4,320 combinations in the alphabet; and it says that these 4,320 parts of the hour are 4,320 breaths that a person breathes, and for every single breath there is a letter of the Name of four letters that gives the life-force of that breath - this is (Deuteronomy 8:3) "for by every utterance of the mouth of the Lord man lives." Since God, blessed be He, is the One who gives breath and life, it is fitting that all his breaths be for the service of the Creator. To this our Sages, of blessed memory, alluded in Bereishit Rabbah (14:9), on the verse (Psalms 150:6) "let every breath [neshamah] praise the Lord" - Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Chanina: for every single breath one breathes, one must praise the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, "let every breath [neshimah] praise the Lord" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:33: When a person contemplates this matter, he will fear sinning and conduct himself with humility and lowliness, for how could he sin and treat lightly the life that God, blessed be He, Who is Ma"h, bestows within him? My teacher, peace be upon him, used to say that concerning this, in the books of the Heichalot (Rabbati, chapter 18, paragraph 4), God, blessed be He, is called "the insulted King," for there is no greater insult than this - that with the very life He, blessed be He, bestows within a person, and with the limbs He prepared for him to serve Him, he sins against Him. He would compare this to a king who gave his servant money to buy bread to sustain himself, and the servant came and bought with the money a stick to strike his master - is there a worse servant than this? And yet God, blessed be He, is "insulted" and overlooks the offense and is slow to anger - how much more so should one formed from a putrid drop refrain from transgressing His attributes, as we shall elaborate, with the Lord's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:34: Rashbi, peace be upon him, summarized all the blemishes in these brief words (Naso 122a) - his words: "whoever transgresses the commandments of the Torah, as it were, causes a blemish above, a blemish below, a blemish to himself, a blemish to all the worlds, which separate his days," etc. - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:1: There are further particulars concerning the fear stemming from judgment: one must fear the several witnesses who testify against him every day, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Chagigah 16a), on the verse (Micah 7:5) "do not trust a friend [rea]" - Rabbi Yehudah bar Nechemiah, the interpreter for Reish Lakish, expounded: what is meant by "do not trust a rea, do not rely on a chief [aluf]"? If your evil inclination [yetzer hara, a play on "rea"] tells you, "sin, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will forgive you," do not believe it, as it is said "do not trust a rea" - and "rea" refers only to the evil inclination, as it is said (Genesis 8:21) "for the inclination of man's heart is evil [ra] from his youth"; and "aluf" [chief/master] refers only to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Jeremiah 3:4) "you are the master [aluf] of my youth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:2: Lest a person say, who testifies against me? The stones of his house and the beams of his house testify against him, as it is said (Habakkuk 2:11) "for the stone shall cry out from the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it." Rabbi Shila said, the two ministering angels who accompany a person testify against him, as it is said (Psalms 91:11) "for He shall command His angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways." Rabbi Chidka says, a person's own soul testifies against him, as it is said (Micah 7:5) "guard the openings of your mouth from her who lies in your bosom" - what is it that lies in a person's bosom? You must say, this is the soul. And the Sages say, a person's own limbs testify against him, as it is said (Isaiah 43:12) "and you are My witnesses, says the Lord, and I am God" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:3: In Ra'aya Meheimna (Shoftim 275a), this passage is explained - their words: "and therefore the masters of the Mishnah established: who testifies against a person? The beams of his house - and not only this, but the members of his household testify against him as well. What are 'the beams of his house'? These are the beams of the heart - (Isaiah 38:2) 'and Hezekiah turned his face to the wall' - this teaches that Hezekiah prayed from the beams [chambers] of his heart. 'The members of his household' are his two hundred and forty-eight limbs, for the masters of the Mishnah established: the sins of a wicked person are engraved upon his bones - and concerning this it is said, who testifies against a person? The beams of his house. And [these] bones are built upon the brain, which is water, and concerning them it hints (Psalms 104:3) 'who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters' - 'lays the beams' [hamekareh] denotes beams [korot]. And why are they [the sins] engraved on the bones more than on flesh, sinews, and skin? Because the bones are white, and the black writing is recognized only by contrast with the white - like the Torah, which is white within, black without: white within is light and darkness, and there is a darkness that is blue [techelet], of which it is said (Psalms 139:12) 'even darkness is not too dark for You,' and techelet is female in relation to the white."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:4: Not only this, but the body is destined to be resurrected upon the bones, and therefore his merits and his sins are engraved on his bones; and if he merits, the body will be resurrected upon his bones, and if not, it will not be resurrected, and he will almost have no share in the resurrection of the dead. Not only this, but there are two witnesses against a person - an eye that sees and an ear that hears - and a court that records and judges his sins; and not only this, but the sun and moon testify against a person, as they have established, etc. - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:5: Now, from the introduction of this passage, which says that the sins of the wicked are engraved on his bones and that he almost has no share in the resurrection, we understand (Proverbs 5:11-12) "and you shall groan at your end, when your flesh and your body are consumed, and you shall say, how I have hated discipline." The matter is that any ordinary person, even a righteous one, has no pain except while the garment of flesh remains intact, for "the worm is as hard for the dead as a needle in living flesh," as it is said (Job 14:22) "but his flesh upon him has pain, and his soul within him mourns"; and as I explained at the end of chapter 12 of this Gate, that after the flesh is decomposed, the righteous has rest and "a loosening of the bones," as it is said (Isaiah 58:11) "and He will loosen your bones." But the wicked, after the judgment of the flesh and the judgment of the grave, retains his sins on his bones, and then he groans and says, "how I have hated discipline," etc. - this is [the meaning of] "at your end, when your flesh and your body are consumed" - this being the end of the flesh's consumption in the grave - "and you shall say," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:6: Further, "your flesh and your body" [besarcha ushe'ercha] may indicate to us that all the desires of this world are transient and perishable, the reason being that the flesh is from the kelipah, and therefore decay rules over it - except for the completely righteous, who purify their flesh in this world, over whom the worm has no power at their death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:7: Now, the primary limbs that desire physical pleasure are through the covenant [brit], and the covenant is called "flesh," as it is said (Jeremiah 11:15) "and holy flesh has passed from you"; and one desires his wife, who is called "she'er" [flesh/kin], as it says (Leviticus 21:2) "but for his kin [she'ero], who is near to him," and our Sages, of blessed memory, explain that "she'ero" refers only to his wife. When a person considers that all the limbs that desire pleasure will be annulled and perish, he will come to refrain from pursuing the vanities of this world, which perish and are destroyed; and this is what is intended by "besarcha" [your flesh] and "she'ercha" [your body/kin]. He says "besarcha" in the second person to indicate that the flesh a person builds up by being drawn after the vanities of the world decays and perishes, but one who sanctifies his flesh and derives pleasure only from a meal of a mitzvah, as I explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 15 - that flesh is not ruled over by the kelipah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:8: Along these lines we understand the verse (Job 14:22) "but his flesh upon him has pain": the flesh he built up is what pains him, "and his soul within him mourns" - how the kelipah drew upon him. But the flesh built up through meals of a mitzvah has no pain upon it and his soul does not mourn, God forbid - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:9: The statement of Rabbi Shila, that the angels who accompany him are the ones who testify against him, appears to correspond to the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Vayeshev 191a) - his words: "and nonetheless, a person must examine his sins every single day, for when a person rises from his bed, two witnesses stand before him and go with him all day. When a person is about to stand up, these witnesses say to him, at the moment he opens his eyes, 'let your eyes look straight ahead and your eyelids look right in front of you' (Proverbs 4:25). He stands up and prepares his feet to walk, and these witnesses say to him, 'make level the path of your feet,' etc. And therefore, as a person goes about each day, he must guard himself from his sins each and every day; when night comes, he must examine and check everything he did that whole day, so that he may repent of it, and gaze upon them constantly, so that he repent before his Master, along the lines of (Psalms 51:5) 'and my sin is always before me,' so that he may repent of it" - so far. Here it explicitly says that the witnesses who warn and testify against him are the two angels.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:10: At the end of the portion of Shelach Lecha (175b), it further adds: he rises to speak, the witnesses say (Psalms 34:14) "guard your tongue from evil," etc.; he stretches out his hands for the affairs of the world, the witnesses say (ibid. 34:15) "turn away from evil and do good" - if he heeds them, well and good; if not, it is written (Zechariah 3:1) "and Satan stood at his right hand to accuse him" - all of them testify against him regarding his sins above; if a person wishes to occupy himself with the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, they all become defending witnesses before Him, standing ready to testify favorably for him at the time he needs it - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:11: Further, Rashbi adds the testimony of the Torah, which testifies against him, the reason being that it is written (Deuteronomy 31:26) "take this book of the Torah... that it may be there as a witness against you." His words (Vayechi 227a), concerning "in four periods the world is judged," say there that in these four periods human beings are judged, and it says afterward: and every single day the books are opened and the deeds are written, and no one pays heed and no one lends his ear, and the Torah testifies against him every day, and a voice cries out loudly (Proverbs 9:4) "whoever is simple, let him turn in here" - "he who lacks understanding," she says to him - and no one heeds her voice. We learn: at the time a person rises in the morning, witnesses stand before him and testify against him, and he pays no heed; the soul testifies before him at every moment and every hour - if he heeds, well and good, and if not, behold, the books are opened and the deeds are written - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:12: He says further on there: we learn, at the time a person is judged above, his soul ascends to the court and they judge concerning its statements, and it testifies to everything, and testifies to all a person's thoughts, but concerning deeds it does not testify, since they are all already written in the book - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:13: Our Sages, of blessed memory, explain something similar in the Yalkut (Mishlei, remez 959), in Pesikta Rabbati, on the verse (Proverbs 20:27) "the candle of the Lord is the soul of man" - Rabbi Acha said: the soul reports every single thing a person does, in secret and in the dark and openly, and ledgers are written before the Holy One, blessed be He, of what human beings do; in the future to come, the Holy One, blessed be He, will rebuke each and every one for his deeds, and they will stand astonished. A parable of one who was married to a king's daughter, and would rise early and inquire after the king's welfare every day, and the king would say to him, "you did such and such in your house, you were angry in such and such a way, you struck your servants in such and such a way"; and he would go out and say to his household, "who told him that I did this? How does he know?" They said to him, "fool of the world, you are married to his daughter, and you ask how he knows? His daughter reports to him." So too the soul - "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Genesis 2:7) - and it reports to Him everything the person does - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:14: Further, it is explained in the Tikkunim (142b) that the Shechinah testifies concerning deeds done in secret - their words: "and there are sins that are done in secret, which the angels who accompany the soul cannot testify to, of whom it is said (Psalms 91:11) 'for He shall command His angels concerning you' - but the Shechinah testifies concerning them, as it is said (Jeremiah 23:24) 'if a man hides himself in secret places,' because the Shechinah is above his head, of whom it is said (Avot, chapter 2, mishnah 1) 'know what is above you' - an eye that sees, and an ear that hears, and all your deeds are written in a book" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:15: Besides the Shechinah testifying concerning deeds done in secret, she also testifies concerning all deeds, even public ones. This is [derived from] the covenant that Joshua made with the children of Israel at Shechem, of which it is said there (Joshua 24:26) "and he took a great stone and set it up there under the oak that was in the sanctuary of the Lord," and it says (ibid. 24:27) "and Joshua said to all the people, behold, this stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words of the Lord which He spoke with us, and it shall be a witness against you, lest you deny your God." According to the plain sense, this verse is difficult to understand; rather, the matter is that this stone is a hint to the "testing stone, the precious cornerstone, the Rock of Israel," which is the Shechinah, and therefore "it heard" and "it is a witness," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:16: Rashbi, peace be upon him, further explains this (Vayechi 222b): we learn, Rabbi Shimon opened and said, (Deuteronomy 29:28) "the hidden things belong to the Lord our God," etc. - "the hidden things": come and see how much a person must guard against his sins and take care not to transgress the will of his Master, for we learn that everything a person does in this world is written in a book, and these deeds enter into the reckoning before the Holy King, and everything is revealed before Him - this is [the meaning of] "if a man hides himself in secret places, shall I not see him? says the Lord." If so, how could a person fail to guard himself against sinning before his Master? And we learn that even what a person merely thinks and arises in his desire, all of it is guarded before the Holy One, blessed be He, and is not lost from Him - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:17: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, explain in the Sifrei, and likewise it is explained in the Tikkunim, that heaven and earth are witnesses to the deeds of man - their words in the Sifrei (Yalkut, portion of Ha'azinu, remez 868): another interpretation, "give ear, O heavens" - Rabbi Bana'ah used to say, when a person is condemned, none lay hands upon him except his witnesses first, as it is said (Deuteronomy 17:7) "the hand of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death," and afterward the people join in, and the hand of all the people is last. So too, when Israel does not do the will of the Omnipresent, what is said of them? (ibid. 11:17) "and He will restrain the heavens," and afterward punishment approaches and comes, as it is said, "and you shall perish quickly." And when Israel does the will of the Omnipresent, what is said of them? (Hosea 2:23) "and it shall come to pass on that day, says the Lord, I will answer the heavens, and they shall answer the earth, and the earth shall answer the grain," etc. - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:18: In the Tikkunim it says: and as it is said, there is testimony in the lower world, as it is said (Lamentations 2:13) "what shall I take to witness for you, what shall I liken to you"; there is testimony in heaven and earth, as it is said (Deuteronomy 30:19) "I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:19: So too in Ra'aya Meheimna (Shoftim 275a): further, the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah are witnesses against a person - this is [the meaning of] "I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day" - "heaven" is that of which it is said (I Kings 8:30) "and You shall hear in heaven"; "and earth" is that of which it is said (Isaiah 66:1) "and the earth is My footstool." Further, there are two [more] witnesses: the central pillar [Tiferet] and Tzaddik [Yesod], and they are "Ed" from "Shema Yisrael... echad" and "Ed" from "Baruch shem kevod malchuto le'olam va'ed" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:20: One must also fear the judgment that is stretched over him every day and every hour, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Rosh Hashanah 16a), on the verse (Job 7:18) "and You visit him every morning, and try him every moment" - it is taught, Rabbi Yosi says, a person is judged every day, as it is said "and You visit him every morning"; Rabbi Natan says, every hour, as it is said "try him every moment"; Rav Chisda said, this is derived from here (I Kings 8:59) "to do justice for His servant and justice for His people Israel, as each day requires" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:21: Further, they said in Tractate Shabbat, chapter 2 (32a): our Rabbis taught, one who falls ill and approaches death is told, "confess," for such is the way of all who are about to die - they confess. When a person goes out into the marketplace, he should regard himself as one handed over to a guard; if his head aches, he should regard himself as one placed in a collar; if he takes to his bed and falls ill, he should regard himself as one brought up to the scaffold for judgment - if he has great advocates, he is saved, and if not, he is not saved. These are a person's great advocates: repentance and good deeds - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:22: Further, they said, of blessed memory (Midrash Tehillim 17), on the verse (Psalms 17:8) "guard me as the apple of the eye [ishon bat ayin]" - Rabbi Elazar said, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: My candle is in your hand and your candle is in My hand. My candle is in your hand - (Proverbs 6:23) "for the commandment is a candle and the Torah is light"; your candle is in My hand - (ibid. 20:27) "the candle of the Lord is the soul of man" - if you guard Mine, I will guard yours - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:23: In the Zohar, portion of Tzav (30b) - his words: "Rabbi Chizkiyah opened, (Psalms 145:17) 'the Lord is righteous in all His ways and pious in all His works.' 'The Lord is righteous in all His ways' - we learn how much human beings must gaze upon the glory of their Master and not stray outward from their path, for every single day judgment hangs over the world, because the world was created and stands upon judgment. Therefore a person must guard himself against his sins, since he does not know the time judgment rests upon him - he sits in his house, judgment rests upon him; he goes out of his house, judgment rests upon him, and he does not know whether he will return to his house or not; he goes out onto the road, how much more so, for then judgment goes forth before him, as it is said (ibid. 85:14) 'righteousness shall go before Him.' Therefore a person must bring mercy first before the King, so that he be saved from the judgment at the time it rests upon the world, for every single day judgment rests upon the world, as it is said (ibid. 7:12) 'and God is angry every day'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:24: Further (Korach 177a), Rabbi Chiya opened, (Proverbs 16:14) "the wrath of a king is as messengers of death, but a wise man will appease it." How much must human beings guard against their sins and watch their deeds, for every single day deeds ascend on a scale and are examined above and are written before Him; and therefore a person must be careful of his sins, for how many times the world is judged - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:25: One must also fear that in the measure a person measures, so it is measured to him: if he overcomes his inclination, he causes the side of kindness to prevail over the side of judgment, and then good comes to him; and if, God forbid, he does the opposite, he causes the side of judgment to prevail over him, and then sufferings come upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:26: Along these lines, it is explained in the Tikkunim (93b) - their words: "and why is he called Metatron, [from] 'matteh' [staff/rod]? Because sometimes he inclines [mateh] toward merit for the righteous, and sometimes inclines toward guilt for the wicked; and therefore he transforms from a staff into a serpent for the wicked, to strike them with it, and from a serpent into a staff for the righteous, to give them reward with it - for this angel is to the Holy One, blessed be He, like the soul that rides upon the body; and the righteous, in this respect, it is said of him (II Samuel 23:3) 'a righteous ruler, the fear of God,' because he transforms judgment into mercy, and in this respect a change of deed is needed to transform judgment into mercy, and a change of name and a change of place. And the Holy One, blessed be He, who is within, of Him it is said (Malachi 3:6) 'I am the Lord, I have not changed,' for He is merciful and gracious, having no judgment at all and no changes; and when a person rules over his inclination, the serpent transforms into a staff, and if his inclination rules over him, the staff transforms into a serpent" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:27: Further, concerning "in the measure a person measures, so it is measured to him," it means that according to the measure of judgment aroused above, that very same measure is bestowed upon the outer forces to exact payment from him; and this is (Job 34:11) "for according to the deed of a man He repays him," as Rashbi explains (Korach 177a) - his words: "'for according to the deed of a man He repays him' - a person goes about in this world and does his deeds and sins before his Master; that deed hangs over him to repay him with judgment - this is [the meaning of] 'for according to the deed of a man He repays him' - that deed shall repay him. Nevertheless, if he sets his heart upon it - once a person sets his heart and his desire on returning before his Master - 'his spirit and his soul He gathers to Himself,' into the bond of life, and does not abandon his soul outside to be judged by another judgment."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:28: This is also explained in the Tikkunim (12a), concerning (Jeremiah 5:22) "who has placed the sand as a boundary for the sea" - their words: "'the sea' is nothing but the Torah; whoever transgresses it is as though he returned the world to chaos and void [tohu vavohu]; and the Sabbath is equal to the whole Torah - whoever transgresses it is as though he returned the world to tohu vavohu, and therefore the verse ["Bereishit yare Shabbat"] is placed near it, (Genesis 1:2) 'and the earth was tohu vavohu' - the sand is to the sea like the chain-link to a dog: whoever removes it from its chain causes several painful bites for himself that it bites him; and concerning it David said (Psalms 22:21) 'save my soul from the sword, my only one, from the power of the dog' - this is Samael, who is caught in the collar," etc. - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:29: With this we understand the punishment for transgressing any negative commandment in the Torah: for the negative commandments are fences and safeguards to hold Samael in his collar and prevent him from being loosed, and one who transgresses loosens the rope, and therefore brings evil upon himself - being bitten with sufferings in this world, or in the World to Come if he was not disciplined in this world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:30: So too it says further in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu (Rabbah, chapter 11), on the verse (I Samuel 6:19) "and He struck the men of Beit Shemesh" - his words: "in everything, the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts payment measure for measure. Because the sons of Eli were corrupt in their deeds, they went out to war and four thousand of Israel were killed. Israel said, why has the Lord defeated us? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: when they were angering Me in the courtyard of Israel and the courtyard of the women, did you not say this? They sent and brought the Ark of the Covenant and sounded a great blast that had no substance to it; concerning that time it is said (Jeremiah 12:8) 'she has raised her voice against Me, therefore I have hated her.' Immediately thirty thousand were killed and the Ark of the Covenant was captured."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:31: And even among the Philistines there was a great plague, as it is said (I Samuel 6:2) "and the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners." And although the priests were worshipers of idolatry, they nevertheless had a sense of proper conduct, saying, "do not send it away empty." And when it [the Ark] was returning on the way to Beit Shemesh, and they were about two thousand cubits, by measure, from Beit Shemesh, they said, let us remove the coverings and place them in a modest place, and let us see what they do for their God, since we have so honored it [the Ark]; and so they did - they took their garments and placed them in a hidden place they had.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:32: The men of Beit Shemesh, once they saw the Ark, should have taken their garments and placed them over their faces and fallen before it for an hour, or two, or three, until the Ark of the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, was covered. But they did not do so - rather, when they saw the Ark, they were laughing and standing up straight and dancing and speaking excessive words, as it is said (I Samuel 6:13) "and the men of Beit Shemesh were reaping," etc., "and they took the Ark and went their way." Therefore fifty thousand of Israel fell, along with the Great Sanhedrin among them, as it is said, "and He struck the men of Beit Shemesh," etc. And who killed all these men of Beit Shemesh? They killed themselves, because they had no proper conduct. From this they said, "in the measure a person measures," etc. Truly, Master of the worlds, (Psalms 36:7) "Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains, Your judgments are a great deep" - so far.
